source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, "Swine Health Management, Volume 3: Frequently Asked Questions on Pig Biosecurity and Disease Reporting", RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012. Acknowledgements credit national focal points from Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam as contributors.
text: A practical farm-level biosecurity checklist for pig producers: locate the farm at least one kilometre from other pig farms, live-animal markets, abattoirs or stockyards where feasible; put up a perimeter fence with no gaps that stray livestock or wild animals could use to enter; avoid planting fruit trees near pig housing, since fruit attracts fruit bats into the area; keep a visitor log book; require visitors to wash hands and change into clean clothing/footwear before entering, and keep their movement through the pig area to a minimum; do not allow farm workers to also raise pigs at their own homes, since this creates a second exposure pathway; new stock should be bought from as few source herds as possible (ideally one) and quarantined for 15-30 days before joining the main herd; group pigs by age and production stage rather than mixing; never sell sick pigs; and bury dead pigs at a depth of more than 1 meter, or burn them, rather than disposing of them informally.
